topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly define Conditional Probability P(A|B) using a Venn Diagram animation. Explain it as 'shrinking the universe' to focus only on event B.
sections.example: Visualizing a drawer of socks: If we know a sock is blue (Event B), what is the probability it is silk (Event A)?

sections.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Rule
sections.content: Define independence as P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate that knowing B provides zero new information about the occurrence of A.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (A) and rolling a die (B). The coin doesn't 'care' what the die shows.

sections.title: The Core of Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a tool to 'reverse' conditional probability. Use an animation showing the transition from P(Evidence|Hypothesis) to P(Hypothesis|Evidence).
sections.example: Medical Testing: If a patient tests positive for a rare disease, what is the actual probability they have it? (Prior probability vs. Posterior probability).

sections.title: Synthesis: Independence vs. Dependency in Bayes
sections.content: Explain how independence simplifies Bayes' calculation. Show how P(A|B) collapses to P(A) when they are independent, removing the 'diagnostic' power of Bayes.
sections.example: Predicting a robot's movement: If the sensor reading is independent of the movement, the Bayes calculation effectively ignores the sensor.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize that Bayes is the engine of modern AI (Naive Bayes classifiers). Emphasize that 'Independence' is an assumption that makes computation efficient but sometimes less accurate.
sections.example: Spam Filters: How your email learns to classify 'Free' (Evidence) as 'Spam' (Hypothesis) using historical probabilities.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a smaller universe.
We shrink the space to event B.
Then, calculate the overlap with event A.
animations: Fade in Venn diagram representing A and B, color A #FF0000.
Animate reduction of sample space to B in blue (#0000FF).
Highlight intersection A and B in purple (#800080).
Label intersection as 'A and B' in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Rule
lecture_lines: Independence means events do not influence each other.
Knowing B tells us nothing about A.
Mathematically, P of A given B equals P of A.
animations: Show two independent events A and B as separate circles.
Fade out circle B to show A remains unchanged.

storyboard.title: The Core of Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: We predict the cause from observed evidence.
The result is a posterior probability.
animations: Animate sliding of terms to reveal Bayesian inversion structure.
Flash entire formula to emphasize the relationship.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: Independence vs. Dependency in Bayes
lecture_lines: When independent, the diagnostic power vanishes.
The formula reduces to the prior probability.
animations: Contrast independent case with dependent case visuals.
Use flow arrows to show influence direction in dependent case.
Fade out influence arrows to show independence.

storyboard.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Bayes is the engine of modern AI.
Naive Bayes assumes features are independent.
It is efficient but sometimes less accurate.
animations: Highlight key takeaways in bold orange (#FFA500).
Fade out display to conclude section.
